title: Talk about plans with skal
objective: Talk about plans with skal + infinitive and a time phrase.
explanation: Danes use “skal” for plans: “Jeg skal arbejde i morgen.” (I'm working tomorrow.) The second verb stays in the infinitive, without “at”. If you start with the time, the verb is still second: “I morgen skal jeg arbejde.” “Hvad skal du i weekenden?” is the classic Friday question.
sourceReference: Deepwater original starter course (2026-10-29), written for Echo; teacher review required before publishing.

exercises.feedbackCorrect: Right: time first, then skal, then jeg.
exercises.feedbackIncorrect: After a time phrase the verb comes second: “I morgen skal jeg …”.

options.text: I morgen jeg skal i biografen.
I morgen skal jeg i biografen.
Jeg i morgen skal i biografen.

exercises.prompt: Complete: “Jeg skal ___ min mor.” (I'm going to visit my mother — at besøge)
exercises.feedbackCorrect: Correct: after skal, use the infinitive “besøge”.
exercises.feedbackIncorrect: After skal, use the infinitive without at: “besøge”.

exercises.prompt: Ask: “What are you doing at the weekend?” — “Hvad ___ du i weekenden?”
Write three sentences about your plans this week, starting at least one with a time phrase (i morgen, på lørdag, i aften).
